headline: Hormuz Tensions and Fading Rate-Hike Bets Set the Stage for Friday's Open
body_html:
Traders arrive at their desks Friday morning navigating a combustible mix of geopolitical risk and shifting monetary expectations. Oil prices pushed higher overnight after Washington vowed it could sustain a naval blockade of Iran indefinitely and threatened measures the Treasury secretary described as unprecedented. The UAE confirmed that two ADNOC vessels were struck by Iranian forces in the Strait of Hormuz, a flashpoint that tightened shipping traffic and renewed questions about whether global petroleum stockpiles are sufficient to absorb a prolonged disruption.

Against that backdrop, Asian equity markets are nonetheless on course for strong weekly gains, with fading bets on further U.S. rate increases offering a cushion. Thursday's session on this side of the Atlantic closed with a constructive tilt — 302 names advanced against 245 decliners across the 549-stock universe — as Software led all sectors with a 2.75% gain while Materials shed 0.90% to finish last.

At the open, watch energy-linked names given the Hormuz developments and crude's overnight move. Software momentum, which powered several double-digit movers on Thursday, will be tested against any risk-off impulse tied to Middle East headlines. Networking hardware, bruised by an 8.40% slide in Cisco on Thursday, faces continued scrutiny.

briefs.headline: Washington Vows Open-Ended Iran Naval Blockade
briefs.body: Senior U.S. officials stated the Navy has the capacity to maintain its blockade of Iran without a defined end date, coupling the announcement with pledges of additional economic pressure. Treasury Secretary Bessent signaled measures not previously deployed against any adversary, rattling oil markets and lifting crude prices ahead of the New York open.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Shipping Lanes Pinched as UAE Reports Vessel Attacks
briefs.body: The UAE said Iranian forces struck two tankers operated by Abu Dhabi National Oil Company in the Strait of Hormuz, though no injuries were reported. The incident constricted traffic through one of the world's most critical energy chokepoints and adds urgency to debates over whether existing oil inventories can weather six or more months of conflict.

briefs.headline: Asian Shares Eye a Strong Weekly Close Despite Regional Jitters
briefs.body: Broader Asian equity indexes were tracking toward meaningful weekly gains Friday as expectations for additional U.S. rate increases continued to recede. Indian shares bucked the regional trend, slipping on reports that Washington threatened an indefinite naval cordon around Iran, a development with direct implications for South Asian energy import costs.

briefs.headline: Iran Conflict Accelerates Chinese Electric-Truck Exports
briefs.body: Analysts note that sustained hostilities in the Middle East are proving an unexpected tailwind for China's electric commercial-vehicle sector, as fuel-cost uncertainty prompts logistics operators to accelerate fleet electrification. Chinese e-truck makers are reportedly capitalizing on the export opportunity, deepening their presence in markets traditionally supplied by petroleum-dependent fleets.

briefs.headline: Trump Administration Reshapes Navy Procurement and Carrier Design
briefs.body: The White House authorized the Pentagon to commission warship construction at foreign yards for the first time in decades, a move framed as a stopgap to close capacity gaps in the U.S. fleet. Separately, an order directing a return to steam-powered catapult systems on aircraft carriers signals a reversal of a costly modernization program pursued under prior administrations.

briefs.headline: Software Names Dominate Thursday's Leaderboard With Double-Digit Moves
briefs.body: Four software or software-adjacent companies posted gains exceeding 10% in Thursday's session, helping the sector outperform every other group by a wide margin. N-able surged 13.58% and ZoomInfo climbed 11.66%, while BlackLine and Docusign each added more than 10%, collectively signaling renewed appetite for enterprise-technology names heading into Friday's open.
